question: Main aim of Green Revolution was to ______.

options.text: increase the production of High Yielding Variety of food crops
decrease the consumption of Chloro Floro Chemicals
increase the total area of land

solution:
The main aim of the Green Revolution was __**to increase the production of a high-yielding variety of food crops.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution was started in India in 1965-68.
 
• The Green Revolution is referred to as a period when Indian agriculture was converted into an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technologies.
 
• Indian agriculture made a transition from old and manual methods and new, innovative and technological methods.
 
• It included the use of products like High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers which were either not used or used on a very limited scale.
 
• The Indian Green Revolution was the brainchild of M.S. Swaminathan. 
 
• M.S. Swaminathan is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• This revolution led to an increase in food grain production especially in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesd.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ Frist Green Revolution In India

 
• The Green Revolution started in the year 1965.
 
• It was the first time when High Yield Variety seeds were introduced in Indian Agriculture.
 
• The main aim of the Green Revolution was to make India self-sufficient when it came to food grains.
 
• This revolution increased production by 500% in North Indian states like Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, and Haryana.
